item.subject: science
item.stem: Meera's class in Nagpur visits a pond where tiny plant-like organisms called microalgae grow. Her teacher explains that these microalgae use sunlight to make their own food. Why does Meera's teacher say that conserving microalgae matters?

options.A: Microalgae add nitrogen to the air when they make food using sunlight.
options.B: Microalgae help maintain oxygen balance and support food security and livelihoods.
options.C: Microalgae can keep making their own food using sunlight even in permanent darkness.
options.D: Conserving microalgae increases pollution because abundant microalgae cause it.
